title: RLC Resonance: Where the Reactances Cancel
topic: Series RLC circuit. Sweep frequency and watch the current peak at f_0 = 1/(2π√LC) where X_L and X_C exactly cancel; phasors visibly oppose at resonance.

beats.narration: Why does a tiny tuning capacitor pick out exactly one radio station from the noise of all of them at once?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre
One frequency, all the rest hushed.

beats.narration: A series circuit with a resistor, an inductor, and a capacitor, driven by an AC source. Tune the source frequency, and watch the current.

elements.content: AC source on left vertical (circle with sine glyph)
Resistor R on top wire
Inductor L coil on right vertical (upper)
Capacitor C plates on right vertical (lower)
Source label e(t) = V₀ cos(ωt)
Z = R + j(ωL − 1/ωC)

beats.narration: Sweep the frequency from low to high. The current is tiny at the extremes — at low omega the capacitor blocks it, at high omega the inductor does — and peaks where the two reactances exactly cancel. That sweet spot is the resonant frequency.

elements.content: Horizontal log-style frequency axis, vertical |I| axis
Resonance curve traces in as the cursor sweeps left-to-right
Frequency cursor (vertical dashed line) that moves with localTime
Peak marker dot at f_0 with label V/R

beats.narration: At resonance, the voltages across the inductor and capacitor are equal in size but pointed opposite ways. They cancel — leaving the resistor alone to set the current, so the impedance collapses to just R.

elements.content: Three phasor diagrams: below, at, above f_0
Below f_0: V_C dominates, net impedance is capacitive
At f_0: V_L + V_C = 0, only V_R remains
Above f_0: V_L dominates, net impedance is inductive

beats.narration: Resonance is the heart of every tuner. Pick L and C to land the peak where you want — and that one frequency wins.

elements.content: Resonance picks one frequency out of the crowd.
every radio, every oscilloscope trigger, every quartz watch
